record.original_question: Let E be a singular point of the moduli space of stable sheaves on surfaces. Suppose the second-order terms in a defining equation do not suffice to decide whether that singularity is canonical. Is there a way to evaluate the third-order or higher-order terms in the defining equation, and can such a method be used to determine whether the singularity is canonical?

evidence.quote: Problem 2.1. Let E be a singularity of the moduli space of stable sheaves on surfaces. Suppose that we can not judge whether it is a canonical singularity or not only from the second-order terms in the defining equation. Is there a way to evaluate third order or higher terms in a defining equation? By using this method, can we judge it is a canonical singularity or not?

We can examine the degree-two part of the defining equation of the moduli space from linear map between Ext-modules of sheaves ([10]. cf. [16, Fact 2.2.]). However, examining terms of third order or higher would be more difficult than that.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $X$ be a smooth projective surface over $\mathbb{C}$, and let $M$ denote a moduli space of stable sheaves on $X$ with fixed numerical invariants (e.g., rank and Chern classes). Let $E \in M$ correspond to a stable sheaf, and assume $E$ is a singular point of $M$. Locally analytically, $M$ near $E$ can be described as the zero locus of a Kuranishi-type defining equation (an obstruction map) $\kappa : \mathrm{Ext}^1(E,E) \to \mathrm{Ext}^2(E,E)$, whose homogeneous quadratic part is governed by the Yoneda pairing $\mathrm{Ext}^1(E,E) \otimes \mathrm{Ext}^1(E,E) \to \mathrm{Ext}^2(E,E)$.

A normal singularity $(Y,p)$ is called canonical if for any resolution $\pi : \widetilde{Y} \to Y$ with $K_{\widetilde{Y}} = \pi^* K_Y + \sum a_i E_i$, all discrepancies $a_i \ge 0$.

Suppose that the quadratic (second-order) part of the defining equation of $M$ at $E$ is not sufficient to determine whether $(M,E)$ is a canonical singularity. Provide a method to compute and evaluate the third-order or higher-order terms of the defining equation in terms of higher Massey-type products on $\mathrm{Ext}^*(E,E)$, and use this method to decide whether the singularity at $E$ is canonical.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as an open research problem about analyzing higher-order obstruction terms in the defining equations of moduli of stable sheaves on surfaces. Existing literature (e.g., Yamada's work on Enriques and hyper-elliptic surfaces) handles canonicity via the second-order/quadratic obstruction part of the Kuranishi map when the expected dimension is sufficiently large, but no general method evaluating third- or higher-order terms to decide canonicity appears in the literature. No source found resolves this in general.

status_evidence.title: Singularities and Kodaira dimension of moduli scheme of stable sheaves on Enriques surfaces
status_evidence.snippet: For moduli schemes of stable sheaves with fixed Chern classes on Enriques surfaces, if the expected dimension is sufficiently large, then the moduli scheme admits only canonical singularities.
status_evidence.claim: Canonicity of singularities of moduli of stable sheaves has been studied through quadratic obstruction terms, leaving higher-order analysis open.

status_evidence.title: The Geometry of Moduli Spaces of Sheaves (Huybrechts–Lehn)
status_evidence.snippet: Local structure of moduli of sheaves is governed by a Kuranishi map whose leading term is the Yoneda pairing on Ext^1.
status_evidence.claim: The standard framework analyzes only the quadratic part of the defining equations via the Yoneda/Ext pairing.
